intl.title: BHSU - International Students (undergraduate application steps, English proficiency, costs, scholarships)

test_policy.notes: BHSU says it is wholly test optional: scores are not required if the student meets another minimum (cumulative GPA 2.6 or top 60% of class); an ACT composite of 18 (SAT 970) also qualifies. Scores may be used for some scholarship eligibility and for initial math and English placement.

requirements.notes: International undergraduate steps: online application with $25 fee (not waived for financial inability); official transcripts mailed to BHSU International Relations (first-time freshman GPA 2.6 on a 4.0 scale); English proficiency scores sent by the testing agency; passport copy; bank statement or letter showing funds for one academic year; I-20 request form. College Navigator lists the domestic application fee as $20 (2024-25). Admission also expects 4 years English, 3 math, 3 lab science, 3 social science and 1 fine arts with a 2.0 GPA. Essay and recommendations are not considered per IPEDS.

deadlines.label: International application deadline, fall 2027 entry (students who need a visa)
deadlines.notes: International page prints 'Fall Enrollment: June 1' with no year (treated as fall 2027); spring enrollment is Nov. 1. The page says the deadline can be extended for applicants already in the U.S. who do not need a visa.

deadlines.label: Scholarships of Distinction: apply for admission before Feb. 1 for full consideration
deadlines.notes: Merit awards of up to $4,000 per year for new first-time students; no separate application. Applicants after Feb. 1 are considered as funds allow. Year not printed; taken as 2027.

deadlines.label: International Scholarship Application priority deadline (fall semester)
deadlines.notes: Priority deadline printed as 'Fall Semester - May 1' (spring semester Oct. 1); students must first be admitted and send final official transcripts. Year not printed; taken as 2027.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exceptions: the student attended secondary or post-secondary school in the U.S. for one academic year; the student is from a native English-speaking country (countries not listed); for some West African countries a WAEC English score above C4. Scores must be sent by the testing agency. Other accepted tests: SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 480, GATEWAY 375, iTEP 3.6. No conditional admission or ESL pathway is described on the page.

cost.notes: Intl page, undergraduate 2026-27: tuition $376.40/credit x 30 = $11,292; general activity fees $1,203; international student fee $400 ($200/semester); discipline fees about $472 (not split out); standard double room $4,338 plus standard meal plan $4,100; health insurance $1,422 (shown in other_usd); books $1,000; total $24,227, excluding $2,000-$5,000 personal spending per semester. SD resident tuition $8,024 from the Tuition & Fees page; that page's financial-aid cost of attendance for a nonresident living on campus is $29,356 (includes miscellaneous and transportation).

aid.notes: F-1 students are eligible for the Global Ambassador Scholarship (competitive, international-only; free on-campus housing for up to eight semesters, estimated at about $14,000 over four years; chosen on essay, GPA, test scores and activities) and for Scholarships of Distinction (up to $4,000 per year based on unweighted GPA and/or ACT/SAT). International students are not eligible for federal aid.

majors.program: Business Administration (AACSB-accredited; specializations incl. Accounting, Economics)
majors.notes: Program page lists specializations including Accounting and Agribusiness/Ranch Management; economics is a specialization of the business degree.
